said: The Bank of England's responses, recorded by meridian-bank-of-england's authors on 2026-11-19: its Statistical Interactive Database's CSV of SONIA (IUDSOIA) with its 10th, 25th, 75th and 90th percentiles (IUDZLS6 to IUDZLS9), the SONIA Compounded Index (IUDZOS2) and Bank Rate (IUDBEDR), and of its 27 spot exchange rates against sterling, each from 3 August to 19 November 2026, the body gzipped; and its latest yield curve file, the zip of the current month's workbooks (2 to 18 November 2026). The rates are as received: reproduction of the Database's data is subject to the UK Open Government Licence; SONIA and/or SONIA Compounded Index data licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 and copyright the Governor and Company of the Bank of England (https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/legal). The exchange rates and the yield curves are synthetic (the product owner's item 197): the Bank's exchange rates are excluded from that licence, reproduced under licence from third parties, and its curves' inputs are Bloomberg Finance L.P.'s and Tradeweb's (https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/yield-curves). Each exchange rate is an invented mean-reverting walk around a level of the currency's magnitude, written as the Database writes it (four places, trailing zeros dropped); each workbook's curves are an invented Nelson-Siegel curve per day, its level, slope and curvature mean-reverting walks, the spot sheets its zero rates and the forward sheets its instantaneous forwards at each column's maturity; all from a seeded generator. Every date, header, empty cell and workbook part is as received; nothing else of a replaced value is. Sample data answers each request from them, and the tests read them; a response recorded again has its exchange rates and curves replaced the same way before it is committed.
